name: Timestamp seed (tsSeed)
plain: Records the browser's clock value when collection starts.
meaning: Time value used to order events and to check clock drift against the server.

limits.headline: Can note your browser's clock when it starts collecting data
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when collection starts on the page
can: Check for clock drift against the server
cannot: Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A bot defense script records the browser's clock value when its data collection starts.
story.for_you: You never see it. A security script stamps the time it started collecting traits. That helps the site check that the data it receives is fresh and was not copied from another visit.
story.for_makers: Bot defense vendors use a time seed to stop replay, where an attacker reuses a valid data bundle from a real browser. It also helps measure how long each part of collection took, which separates humans from scripts.

use_cases.example: A bot defense system rejects a data bundle with an old timestamp, since an attacker reused it.
A sneaker or ticket site blocks bots that replay a captured valid session.
A bank checks that device checks were produced on this visit, not copied.
A browser game with prizes blocks replayed session data sent by cheats.
A social site blocks fake sign up scripts that reuse a valid captured bundle.
An ad network rejects click reports with stale or repeated time seeds.
A fraud analytics tool measures time between steps to see if it matches a person.

risks: Hard for honest users to see
